My BigQuery table has more inventory rows than the source ERP. How should I diagnose this? (Variation 0)

Start by separating physical row count from distinct business-key count. A table can have the same distinct inventory IDs but more physical rows because of duplicates.

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
  COUNT(DISTINCT UPPER(TRIM(CAST(`Inventory ID` AS STRING)))) AS distinct_inventory_ids,
  COUNTIF(`Inventory ID` IS NULL) AS null_inventory_ids,
  COUNTIF(TRIM(CAST(`Inventory ID` AS STRING)) = '') AS blank_inventory_ids
FROM `project.dataset.style`;
```

Then find keys duplicated after normalization:

```sql
SELECT
  UPPER(TRIM(CAST(`Inventory ID` AS STRING))) AS inventory_id_norm,
  COUNT(*) AS row_count
FROM `project.dataset.style`
GROUP BY inventory_id_norm
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY row_count DESC;
```

If BigQuery has extra distinct IDs, use `EXCEPT DISTINCT` against the ERP extract. Do not delete anything until you classify whether the extra records are valid new records, inactive records, or sync artifacts.
